data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Sondra (Σονδρη) is derived from the word 'sonder', meaning sun. It was believed that the goddess Helios, the sun, fathered Sondra. The name's Greek roots evoke images of warmth, light, and renewal. The name Sondra carries the meaning “Daughter of the Sun” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Sondra usually hope their child will grow to embody daughter of the sun and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sondra was not particularly common among early Christians, but it did have some noteworthy bearers throughout history. One such famous bearer was Sondra Pride, an African-American gospel singer who achieved significant success in the 20th century. Her powerful voice and uplifting performances brought joy and inspiration to countless lives. Sondra is also the name of an American television character from the science-fiction series "Star Trek: Deep Space Nine". As a Starfleet officer and later a Bajoran religious leader, Sondra represented a bridge between different cultures and belief systems, showcasing the potential for unity and understanding in a diverse universe.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Sondra can be seen as a reflection of the divine light that resides within each individual. Just as the sun provides warmth and illumination to the world, our inner light, often referred to as the 'higher self' or 'spark of divinity', can guide us through life's challenges, bring us comfort, and inspire growth. The spiritual significance of the name Sondra is further enhanced by its connections to the Greek goddess Helios and the eternal sun. Through this symbolism, Sondra serves as a reminder that we are all connected to a source of infinite wisdom, love, and creativity.
